:::{#rem-local-minimizer}
#### Local and global minimizers

For $p = 1$, $\norm{x - x^*} = \abs{x - x^*}$.
For example, with $x^* = 1$ and $\tolin = 1$,
the condition $\abs{x - 1} < 1$ means $0 < x < 2$.

Every [global minimizer](#def-global-minimizer) is a [local minimizer](#def-local-minimizer):
take any $\tolin > 0$.
For example, $x^* = 0$ is a global minimizer of $f(x) = x^2$ on $\reals$,
so it is also a local minimizer.

The [converse](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/proof-writing.html#def-converse) fails.
In @exr-local-vs-global-min,
$x^* = 1$ is a local minimizer of $f(x) = x^3 - 3x$ (take $\tolin = 1$),
but not a global one.

:::
